title: Load balancing — banditx
description: Strategies, sticky sessions, health checks, circuit breaker, retries.
text: ← Back to docs Load balancing Strategies, sticky sessions, health checks, circuit breaker, retries. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 7 min read Selection strategies Weights and backup Sticky sessions Health checks Circuit breaker Retries and timeouts Keep-alive pool An upstream is a pool of identical backends plus rules: how to pick, how to check, what to do on failure. # Selection strategies Strategy When to use round_robin default when backends are identical least_conn when requests have different durations (SSE, streaming) random many backends, doesn't matter who takes the next ip_hash client-to-backend affinity without cookies uri_hash when you need the same cache hit p2c power of two choices — nearly always best p99 yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app strategy: p2c servers: - { addr: 10.0.0.10:8080 } - { addr: 10.0.0.11:8080 } - { addr: 10.0.0.12:8080 } ✓ If in doubt Pick p2c . It's nearly as good as least_conn and resilient to skew. # Weights and backup Heterogeneous machines can be loaded unevenly via weight . Some servers can be backup: true — they take over only if every primary is down. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app servers: - { addr: 10.0.0.10:8080, weight: 5 } - { addr: 10.0.0.11:8080, weight: 2 } - { addr: 10.0.0.12:8080, weight: 1 } - { addr: 10.0.0.20:8080, backup: true } # Sticky sessions When a backend keeps state in memory (sessions, cache), you need client affinity. banditx supports two modes: cookie and IP. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app sticky: mode: cookie cookie_name: BANDITX ttl: 1h secure: true http_only: true same_site: Lax - name: legacy sticky: mode: ip subnet_v4: 24 subnet_v6: 64 # Health checks Active checks are HTTP probes to each backend at a fixed interval. Passive checks watch real traffic (5xx, timeouts). yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app health_check: type: http path: /healthz interval: 5s timeout: 1s method: GET expect_status: [200, 204] expect_body: "^ok" healthy_threshold: 2 unhealthy_threshold: 3 passive: enabled: true fail_window: 30s max_fails: 5 ℹ active + passive Combine both. Active catches a dead process; passive catches degradation under load, when /healthz returns 200 but real requests fail. # Circuit breaker When a backend starts failing consistently, the breaker stops sending traffic for a fixed time. Neighbors in the pool are saved from cascading failure. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app circuit_breaker: enabled: true error_rate_threshold: 0.5 # 50% min_requests: 20 window: 30s open_duration: 60s half_open_probes: 3 # Retries and timeouts Retries are safe only for idempotent requests. banditx retries GET , HEAD , OPTIONS , PUT , DELETE automatically. POST — only if the backend sent zero bytes. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app timeouts: connect: 2s read: 30s write: 30s idle: 60s retries: attempts: 3 backoff: exponential # fixed|exponential base_delay: 50ms max_delay: 1s on_status: [502, 503, 504] # Keep-alive pool Connection reuse to the backend is the cheapest way to boost RPS. On by default, but tune pool size for load. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app keepalive: enabled: true pool_size: 256 # per backend idle_timeout: 90s max_lifetime: 1h Previous ← TLS / ACME Next Metrics & logs →

title: Configuration — banditx
description: A single YAML file. Full schema, every field, examples, env vars.
text: ← Back to docs Configuration A single YAML file. Full schema, every field, examples, env vars. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 8 min read Minimal config Top-level schema The server section The listeners section The upstreams section The routes section Environment variables Validation Hot reload The config is a single banditx.yaml . No include , no scripts, no magic. Everything the proxy does lives in this file. # Minimal config This is enough to proxy example.com to a local backend over HTTPS with built-in ACME. banditx.yaml Копировать server: log_level: info listeners: - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:443 tls: acme: email: admin@example.com domains: [example.com] upstreams: - name: app servers: - addr: 127.0.0.1:8080 routes: - name: main match: host: example.com upstream: app # Top-level schema Section Required Purpose server no global process settings listeners yes what addresses and ports to listen on upstreams yes backend pools, strategies, health checks routes yes routing rules middleware no reusable middleware chains metrics no Prometheus endpoint and log format # The server section yaml Копировать server: workers: 0 # 0 = auto (num CPUs) log_level: info # trace|debug|info|warn|error log_format: json # json|text pid_file: /var/run/banditx.pid grace_period: 15s # how long to wait for active conns on shutdown user: banditx group: banditx max_connections: 100000 ℹ workers: 0 banditx is async (tokio). Instead of forking processes, it spawns worker threads. 0 (auto) is usually the right pick. # The listeners section Each listener is a bind with optional TLS and HTTP/2. For 80 and 443, use two listeners and one redirect route. yaml Копировать listeners: - name: http bind: 0.0.0.0:80 protocol: http http2: false - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:443 protocol: https http2: true http3: false # WIP tls: cert_file: /etc/banditx/certs/fullchain.pem key_file: /etc/banditx/certs/privkey.pem min_version: "1.2" alpn: [h2, http/1.1] # The upstreams section yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app strategy: least_conn # round_robin|least_conn|ip_hash|uri_hash|random|p2c protocol: http # http|https|fastcgi keepalive: enabled: true pool_size: 128 servers: - addr: 10.0.0.10:8080 weight: 3 - addr: 10.0.0.11:8080 weight: 1 backup: false health_check: type: http path: /health interval: 5s timeout: 1s healthy_threshold: 2 unhealthy_threshold: 3 # The routes section Routes are matched top-down. The first one whose rule matches wins. Order in the file matters. yaml Копировать routes: - name: api match: host: api.example.com path_prefix: /v1 upstream: app middleware: - rate_limit: 100/s - cors: "*" - name: static match: path_regex: ^/\.(js|css|png|svg)$ upstream: cdn - name: redirect-http match: listener: http action: redirect to: https://$host$request_uri status: 301 # Environment variables Any value in the config can be substituted from env via ${VAR} or ${VAR:-default} . Useful for secrets and ports. yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: app servers: - addr: ${APP_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${APP_PORT:-8080} listeners: - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:${HTTPS_PORT:-443} tls: acme: email: ${ACME_EMAIL} # Validation Before applying, always run check . It catches typos, dangling references and incompatible flags. bash Копировать banditx check --config ./banditx.yaml # ✓ config ok # 2 listeners, 4 upstreams, 12 routes # 1 warning: unused middleware "old-cors" ⚠ Recursive references If a route references an upstream that references a route — check will fail and refuse to start. By design. # Hot reloa

title: Installation — banditx
description: Install banditx: binary, Docker, cargo, systemd. Takes under a minute.
text: ← Back to docs Installation Install banditx: binary, Docker, cargo, systemd. Takes under a minute. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 5 min read Prebuilt binary Docker From source systemd unit Verify the install Upgrade Uninstall banditx builds into a single static binary . No runtime, no VMs, no package managers. Download, run, done. # Prebuilt binary The fastest path. Grab the tarball for your platform from the latest release and unpack it into /usr/local/bin . terminal Копировать curl -L https://github.com/NormikChel/banditx/releases/latest/download/banditx-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz \ | tar xz -C /usr/local/bin chmod +x /usr/local/bin/banditx banditx --version ℹ Signature check Every release is signed with minisign. The public key is in the repo README. If you're paranoid, verify the hash in SHA256SUMS . # Other platforms macOS (Intel / Apple Silicon) — banditx-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz Windows x64 — banditx-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip Linux ARM64 (RPi 4+, Graviton) — banditx-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz Alpine / musl — banditx-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz # Docker The image is ~12 MB, built from scratch. Only the binary and CA certs inside. docker run Копировать docker run -d \ --name banditx \ --restart unless-stopped \ -p 80:80 -p 443:443 \ -v $(pwd)/banditx.yaml:/etc/banditx/banditx.yaml:ro \ -v $(pwd)/certs:/etc/banditx/certs:ro \ ghcr.io/normikchel/banditx:latest docker-compose.yml Копировать services: banditx: image: ghcr.io/normikchel/banditx:latest restart: unless-stopped ports: - "80:80" - "443:443" volumes: - ./banditx.yaml:/etc/banditx/banditx.yaml:ro - ./certs:/etc/banditx/certs:ro healthcheck: test: ["CMD", "banditx", "health"] interval: 10s # From source Requires Rust 1.78+ and a linker. Builds in ~40 seconds on modern hardware. bash Копировать cargo install --git https://github.com/NormikChel/banditx --locked # or locally git clone https://github.com/NormikChel/banditx cd banditx && cargo build --release ./target/release/banditx --version # systemd unit For production, use a minimal unit with hardening flags. No RuntimeDirectory or User=www-data required — banditx runs unprivileged and binds 80/443 via AmbientCapabilities . /etc/systemd/system/banditx.service Копировать [Unit] Description=banditx reverse proxy After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] Type=simple ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/banditx --config /etc/banditx/banditx.yaml ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID Restart=on-failure RestartSec=2 User=banditx Group=banditx AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE NoNewPrivileges=true ProtectSystem=strict ProtectHome=true PrivateTmp=true PrivateDevices=true ProtectKernelTunables=true ProtectKernelModules=true ProtectControlGroups=true LockPersonality=true MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true SystemCallArchitectures=native [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target bash Копировать sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now banditx sudo systemctl status banditx # Verify the install After start, check three things: version, config validity and the health endpoint. bash Копировать banditx --version banditx check --config /etc/banditx/banditx.yaml curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/healthz ✓ Done If check printed config ok, 12 routes, 4 upstreams — head to Configuration . # Upgrade banditx supports hot reload. Zero-downtime upgrade = unpack the new binary over the old one and send SIGHUP . bash Копировать curl -L https://github.com/NormikChel/banditx/releases/

title: Metrics & logs — banditx
description: Prometheus, ready-made dashboards, structured logs, alerts.
text: ← Back to docs Metrics & logs Prometheus, ready-made dashboards, structured logs, alerts. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 5 min read Prometheus endpoint What's exported PromQL examples Logs Ready-made dashboard Health endpoints banditx exposes Prometheus-format metrics on a dedicated HTTP port. Logs are structured JSON, ready for any parser. # Prometheus endpoint yaml Копировать metrics: enabled: true bind: 127.0.0.1:9090 path: /metrics auth: type: bearer token: ${METRICS_TOKEN} prometheus.yml Копировать scrape_configs: - job_name: banditx scrape_interval: 15s scheme: http authorization: type: Bearer credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/banditx.token static_configs: - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9090"] ⚠ Never bind 0.0.0.0 Default bind is 127.0.0.1:9090 . If you really need external — add auth and firewall. # What's exported Metric Type Description banditx_requests_total counter total requests, labeled by route/status/method banditx_request_duration_seconds histogram latency (buckets: .001 … 10) banditx_request_size_bytes histogram request size banditx_response_size_bytes histogram response size banditx_active_connections gauge open connections banditx_upstream_health gauge 1/0 per backend banditx_upstream_retries_total counter retry count banditx_circuit_breaker_state gauge 0=closed 1=half 2=open banditx_tls_cert_expiry_seconds gauge seconds until cert expiry banditx_build_info gauge version and build hash # PromQL examples RPS per route Копировать sum by (route) (rate(banditx_requests_total[1m])) p99 latency Копировать histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, route) (rate(banditx_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) ) 5xx over 5 minutes Копировать sum(rate(banditx_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(banditx_requests_total[5m])) Alert: backend down Копировать banditx_upstream_health == 0 Alert: cert expiring Копировать banditx_tls_cert_expiry_seconds < 14 * 86400 # Logs Format is JSON Lines. One event per line. Standard fields plus whatever you add in log.fields . yaml Копировать server: log_level: info log_format: json access_log: enabled: true path: /var/log/banditx/access.log fields: - ts - remote_addr - method - host - path - status - bytes_sent - duration_ms - upstream - upstream_addr - user_agent - request_id one access.log line Копировать {"ts":"2026-10-14T19:43:12.384Z","remote_addr":"203.0.113.7","method":"GET","host":"api.example.com","path":"/v1/users/42","status":200,"bytes_sent":384,"duration_ms":7.21,"upstream":"app","upstream_addr":"10.0.0.10:8080","user_agent":"curl/8.5.0","request_id":"01HZ8V4XKJ2T5N" # Ready-made dashboard The repo ships dashboards/banditx.json — one-click import into Grafana. Panels: RPS, p50/p95/p99, error rate, active connections, backend health, cert lifetime. bash Копировать curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NormikChel/banditx/main/dashboards/banditx.json \ -o banditx-dashboard.json # Grafana → Dashboards → Import → Upload JSON # Health endpoints Separate from metrics are two endpoints for load balancers and Kubernetes. Path Purpose /healthz liveness — 200 while the process is alive /readyz readiness — 200 when config is loaded and all critical upstreams are healthy /version JSON with version and git hash bash Копировать curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/healthz && echo curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/readyz && echo curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/version Previous ← Load balancing

title: Routing — banditx
description: Host, path, regex, headers, priorities, redirect and rewrite — with examples.
text: ← Back to docs Routing Host, path, regex, headers, priorities, redirect and rewrite — with examples. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 7 min read What you can match Priorities Redirect and rewrite Headers Copy-paste recipes Routing is the heart of banditx. Rules are simple but expressive. Here's everything that can go into routes: . # What you can match Field Example What it does host api.example.com exact Host match (case-insensitive) host_regex ^.*\.example\.com$ regex against Host path_prefix /v1 path prefix path_regex ^/users/\d+$ regex against path method POST,PUT HTTP method header Authorization: Bearer * header match (glob) query debug=1 query param presence listener http only on a specific listener ℹ AND by default All conditions in one match: are AND-ed. If you need OR — write two routes. # Priorities Rules are processed top-down , the first match wins. Two ways to control order: physical order in the file, or explicit priority . yaml Копировать routes: - name: exact-api priority: 100 # higher = earlier match: host: api.example.com path_prefix: /v1/admin upstream: admin - name: api priority: 50 match: host: api.example.com upstream: app ⚠ Anti-pattern Don't create 30 routes with the same match and different priority . It works, but reading it hurts. Split by listener or subdomain instead. # Redirect and rewrite A route can redirect instead of proxying. Variables supported: $host , $request_uri , $scheme , $remote_addr . yaml Копировать routes: # HTTP → HTTPS - name: force-https match: listener: http action: redirect to: https://$host$request_uri status: 301 # /old/* → /new/* - name: rename match: path_prefix: /old action: rewrite replace: { from: ^/old, to: /new } upstream: app # Headers Headers can be added, overwritten and removed. Both request and response. yaml Копировать routes: - name: with-headers match: { host: example.com } upstream: app request_headers: set: X-Forwarded-Proto: $scheme X-Real-IP: $remote_addr X-Request-Id: $uuid remove: - X-Internal-Token response_headers: set: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff remove: - Server # Copy-paste recipes # SPA with index.html fallback yaml Копировать routes: - name: spa-assets match: { path_prefix: /assets } upstream: static - name: spa-fallback match: { host: app.example.com } action: rewrite replace: { from: ^.*$, to: /index.html } upstream: static # PHP-FPM yaml Копировать upstreams: - name: php protocol: fastcgi servers: - addr: unix:/run/php/php8.3-fpm.sock routes: - name: php-app match: { host: site.example.com } upstream: php fastcgi: document_root: /var/www/site/public script: index.php # WebSocket yaml Копировать routes: - name: ws match: host: ws.example.com header: Upgrade: websocket upstream: realtime websocket: idle_timeout: 300s ping_interval: 30s Previous ← Configuration Next TLS / ACME →

title: TLS / ACME — banditx
description: BYO certs, Let's Encrypt built-in, SNI, mTLS, HSTS.
text: ← Back to docs TLS / ACME BYO certs, Let's Encrypt built-in, SNI, mTLS, HSTS. Updated : 2026-10-14 · 6 min read Static certificates ACME / Let's Encrypt SNI and multiple domains mTLS (client certificates) HSTS and security headers OCSP Stapling banditx handles two scenarios: bring your own certificates, or let Let's Encrypt issue them automatically. Both can coexist: ACME for one domain, a wildcard for another. # Static certificates yaml Копировать listeners: - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:443 protocol: https tls: cert_file: /etc/banditx/certs/fullchain.pem key_file: /etc/banditx/certs/privkey.pem min_version: "1.2" ciphers: modern # modern|intermediate|compat alpn: [h2, http/1.1] ℹ Cert chain order cert_file must contain the chain: leaf first, then intermediates. That's the standard, but people sometimes mix it up with cat server.crt ca.crt . # ACME / Let's Encrypt The built-in ACME client speaks HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01. No certbot, no cron jobs. Certs renew automatically 30 days before expiry. yaml Копировать listeners: - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:443 protocol: https tls: acme: email: admin@example.com domains: - example.com - www.example.com - api.example.com challenge: tls-alpn-01 # or http-01 directory: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory storage: /var/lib/banditx/acme ⚠ Use staging for tests In development, use https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory . LE has strict rate limits and hitting them is easy. # SNI and multiple domains SNI routing serves different certificates to different hosts on one listener. ACME can handle multiple — the proxy picks the right cert. yaml Копировать listeners: - name: https bind: 0.0.0.0:443 protocol: https tls: cert_file: /etc/banditx/certs/wildcard.example.com.pem key_file: /etc/banditx/certs/wildcard.example.com.key acme: email: admin@example.com domains: [partner.com, partner.net] sni: match: true # mTLS (client certificates) For internal APIs, mTLS is a clean way to lock everything down. banditx verifies the chain and (optionally) the CN. yaml Копировать listeners: - name: internal-https bind: 0.0.0.0:8443 protocol: https tls: cert_file: /etc/banditx/certs/server.pem key_file: /etc/banditx/certs/server.key client_auth: mode: require # none|request|require ca_file: /etc/banditx/certs/clients-ca.pem allowed_cn: - "svc-billing" - "svc-auth" # HSTS and security headers yaml Копировать routes: - name: main match: { host: example.com } upstream: app response_headers: set: Strict-Transport-Security: "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin Content-Security-Policy: "default-src 'self'" ✕ preload is hard to undo If you submit to hstspreload.org , removal can take months. Test with max-age=300 first. # OCSP Stapling Enabled by default for static certs. Also on for ACME, no config needed. Previous ← Routing Next Load balancing →

description: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, FastCGI. Reverse proxy, load balancer, health checks, Prometheus metrics — a single binary with no dependencies.
text: Rust · HTTP/1.1 · HTTP/2 · FastCGI · WebSocket Fast reverse proxy. Nginx alternative. A single binary, YAML config, zero dependencies. Proxying, load balancing, health checks, Prometheus metrics — out of the box. Get started → GitHub ~2× faster than nginx on RPS <5 MB binary size 0 runtime dependencies 1 file banditx.yaml config Features → Benchmarks → Compare with nginx →
